title: Senior's toolkit: inspecting and configuring cookies
summary: See cookies in DevTools and curl, read Set-Cookie attributes, and configure ASP.NET Core cookie auth and antiforgery.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: inspecting and configuring cookies
steps.body: Most session bugs are cookie bugs: a cookie that was never set, never sent, or sent where it should not be. These are the tools experienced developers use to see what the browser really does, and the settings they check in ASP.NET Core.

toolkit.what: In Chrome and Edge (Storage in Firefox): every cookie for the site with its flags. The Network tab shows the `Cookie` header each request sent, and warns when the browser blocked a `Set-Cookie`.
flags: check them on the session cookie
what was actually sent, and why others were filtered out
start a clean session while testing

toolkit.what: Drive a cookie login from the terminal: save what the server sets and send it back on the next call. `-i` shows the response headers, including every `Set-Cookie`.
flags: write received cookies to a file
accept the local dev certificate (never against real servers)
toolkit.example:
curl -i -c jar.txt -d 'user=ana&password=secret' https://localhost:5001/login
curl -i -b jar.txt https://localhost:5001/account

toolkit.what: The attributes that make a session cookie safe. Read them in every `Set-Cookie` header you see.
flags: JavaScript cannot read it, so XSS cannot steal it
not sent on cross-site POSTs, which blocks most CSRF
browser enforces Secure, Path=/ and no Domain
toolkit.example: Set-Cookie: __Host-sid=k3J9...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=28800

toolkit.what: ASP.NET Core cookie authentication. Sign in with `HttpContext.SignInAsync`, out with `SignOutAsync`; the cookie holds an encrypted ticket.
flags: renew while the user stays active

toolkit.what: CSRF tokens for form posts. Minimal API endpoints that bind form data (`[FromForm]`, `IFormFile`) are checked automatically (.NET 8+) once `UseAntiforgery()` is in the pipeline; MVC uses `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]` or the global auto-validate filter.
flags: validates the token on form posts
issue a token for your own form or SPA
opt one endpoint out (for example a webhook)

toolkit.what: Clear the auth cookie. With server-side sessions also delete the session record, or a stolen cookie keeps working.
flags: which cookie scheme to sign out of
revoke on the server, not only in the browser

steps.prompt: Match each cookie attribute to what it protects against.
pairs: a script stealing the cookie after an XSS bug
the cookie travelling over plain HTTP
another site making the browser POST with the cookie
a subdomain setting or overriding the cookie

steps.prompt: Login returns 200 and the response has this header, yet the next request from the browser is anonymous. You are testing from your phone at `http://192.168.1.20:5000`. Why?
options: The cookie is `Secure` (and `__Host-` requires it), so the browser never sends it over plain HTTP; use the HTTPS profile
`HttpOnly` stops the browser from storing the cookie
The cookie name is too long
steps.explain: Browsers make an exception for `http://localhost`, but not for other plain-HTTP hosts. DevTools' Network tab shows the blocked cookie with the reason. Test over HTTPS rather than weakening the cookie.

steps.prompt: Log in with curl, keep the cookie, and use it on the next call.
steps.explain: `-c` writes cookies the server sets into the jar; `-b` reads them back and sends them.

steps.prompt: Safe session cookie setting, or a red flag in review?
items: `Cookie.HttpOnly = false` so the SPA can read the session
Logout that only deletes the cookie in JavaScript

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Whenever a login works in one place and not another, open DevTools or `curl -i` and read the `Set-Cookie` header and the cookies actually sent before touching code. In review, check every session cookie for HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and a real server-side logout.
